source.title: "Not"is Not Lost in Translation: A Causal Analysis of Negation Representations in Multilingual LLMs
source.authors: Giang Nguyen; W. Buntine; Dung D. Le; Wen-Ya Wang

record.tranche_reason: The study examines sparse features in multilingual LLMs, an LLM setting beyond the toy networks in the original superposition work. It tests only the sparse-feature/SAE part of V4, not superposition geometry or capacity pressure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports naturally occurring SAE-feature activations on negated and affirmative inputs, which bear on whether SAE dictionaries recover sparse features. The many addition/removal flip rates are produced by deliberate activation steering, so they are not evidence that the models spontaneously exhibit those polarity changes. Probe accuracies are about linear decodability, not SAE features. Values used for layer and feature selection, and results cited from other work, are not recorded as findings.
record.test_reason: The study inspects how often pretrained SAE features fire on negated versus affirmative inputs in three LLMs (Table 16). This is weak, indirect evidence that SAE dictionaries recover a sparse, selective feature, which bears on V4. Superposition itself is never discussed or tested. Most of the paper is steering with dense and SAE directions.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that multilingual LLMs encode negation in a largely shared, causally controllable representation. It is reachable through dense contrastive directions and single SAE features, generalizes to unseen languages and FLORES-derived sentences, and the SAE features respond selectively to negation in every language.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses contrastive activation directions and pretrained SAE decoder features with causal steering in multilingual translation; it does not reproduce the toy-model superposition method or measure feature-over-dimension geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports weaker activation and steering for Llama-3.1-8B on Vietnamese than for its other tested languages. It also reports that only a small number of SAE layers/features show strong steering effects, and that steering depends on empirically selected coefficients.

fits_no_version.finding: A dense contrastive (CAA) negation direction causally flips polarity across languages; per-language directions have cosine 0.48–0.82.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear representation hypothesis: concepts such as negation correspond to shared linear directions in activation space.

fits_no_version.finding: Gemma models have single massive-activation dimensions that dominate direction norms but have no causal role (Table 4–5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Privileged or outlier residual dimensions distort direction-similarity analyses without carrying the concept.

record.problems: The evidence relevant to V4 covers only three models with publicly available pretrained SAEs and one selected SAE feature per model. Llama and Qwen SAEs were trained on base models but applied to instruct-tuned variants. Feature selection and intervention strengths were empirically tuned; the paper’s stated limitations also restrict the analysis to explicit verbal negation and translation. No uncertainty intervals are reported for the feature-activation findings.
record.rows_left_out: CAA and SAE addition/removal flip-rate results in Tables 1–3 and Figures 3–5 are deliberately induced by steering and were not treated as evidence for naturally occurring representation. Linear-probe results in Figures 12–14 measure polarity decodability, not SAE features. Feature-selection sweeps and layer/strength selection results in Appendix D.4–D.5 were not included.

untested.parts: No toy models, no feature-versus-dimension overload, no interference geometry, no sparsity phase transition.
No neuron-level polysemanticity and no capacity or importance allocation.
No test of whether features are spread across many neurons. Only one hand-selected feature per model; no prevalence or dictionary-wide analysis.
No completeness, stability or canonicality tests across SAE widths, seeds or releases. The paper notes only a few layers and features steer effectively.
Uses 1-D decoder directions but never tests one-dimensionality versus multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: Steering rates using a single SAE feature's decoder vector: ≥91% for Gemma and Qwen; Llama VI 72.0/57.1. These show the recovered feature is causally linked to polarity. They are relevant if causal relevance of dictionary features counts toward V4.
Only a few layers (K=10 sweep) and a small fraction of top-ranked features show strong polarity control. This bears on how reliably SAEs recover usable features.

record.verdict_notes: The study does not engage with superposition. The V4 bearing rests only on selectivity counts for three cherry-picked features (selected by steering performance), measured on the extraction split. Treat the evidence as weak. No uncertainty is reported. The SAEs for Llama and Qwen were trained on base models but applied to instruct models.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network test, feature-to-dimension overload, overlap geometry, sparsity transition, or regular geometry.
No capacity competition, neuron polysemanticity, or allocation by feature importance.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity.

Tests selective SAE-feature activations for negation in three instruction-tuned LLMs, but not whether features are generally spread across many neurons, their prevalence across models, or how many SAE features are needed beyond one selected feature per model.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units across dictionaries, training runs, or settings.
Uses decoder vectors as directions, but does not test whether represented features are intrinsically one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Gemma-3-4B
rows.operation_detail: Inspected activations of the EN-selected SAE feature L4 f331 on Mini-minus-4 inputs.
rows.measure: Feature activation patterns on naturally occurring source-token inputs
rows.value: The feature primarily activates at explicit negation markers across languages.
rows.note: The paper gives representative token firing counts in Table 16, but the flattened layout makes some cell assignments uncertain; the qualitative model-specific description is explicit.
rows.check: Value is correct per Table 16 (e.g. not 132/0, không 150/0, pas 150/0, 不 78/0). Some firings on affirmatives exist (很 3/41 in ZH; tôi 29/29 in VI). Baseline is the affirmative-example firing count, not 'not stated'. The counts come from the extraction set, which is the set used to rank the feature by δf, so EN selectivity is partly circular.

source_check.correct: Baseline: affirmative-example token firing counts are reported. Negative/affirmative occurrences include not 132/0, không 150/0, pas 150/0, 不 78/0, tôi 29/29, Tôi 15/15, and 很 3/41. Activations were inspected on 150 negative and 150 affirmative synthetic extraction examples per language.
source_check.problem: The baseline is reported, rather than unstated; some tokens also activate on affirmative examples.

rows.subject: Qwen3.5-9B
rows.operation_detail: Inspected activations of the EN-selected SAE feature L10 f43677 on Mini-minus-4 inputs.
rows.measure: Feature activation patterns on naturally occurring source-token inputs
rows.value: The feature responds to both negation markers and tokens in negated contexts across languages.
rows.note: The paper gives representative token firing counts in Table 16, but the flattened layout makes some cell assignments uncertain; the qualitative model-specific description is explicit.
rows.check: Baseline is the affirmative firing counts from Table 16 (e.g. not 132/0, không 150/0, pas 150/0). The extraction-set circularity noted for r1 applies here too.

source_check.correct: Baseline: affirmative-example token firing counts are reported. Representative negative/affirmative occurrences include not 132/0, không 150/0, pas 150/0, and 不 37/0. These are token firing occurrences on the synthetic extraction set, not sentence-level recovery rates.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Inspected activations of the EN-selected SAE feature L13 f12611 on Mini-minus-4 inputs.
rows.measure: Feature activation patterns on naturally occurring source-token inputs
rows.value: The feature predominantly activates on tokens in negated contexts; its activation is weaker on Vietnamese inputs than on the other languages.
rows.note: The authors identify weaker Vietnamese activation as one explanation for the feature’s weaker causal control on Vietnamese.
rows.check: Partial applies mainly to VI, where firings are very sparse (thích 3/0, đủ 1/0). EN, FR and ZH are selective (e.g. pas 69/0, '.' 83/0), which is closer to observed. The SAE was trained on the base model and applied to the instruct model.

source_check.correct: Baseline: affirmative-example token firing counts are reported. Representative negative/affirmative occurrences are EN period 83/0; VI thích 3/0, đủ 1/0, nghe 1/0; FR pas 69/0; ZH 喜欢 18/0. The partial state reflects weaker Vietnamese activation; the other languages show clearer selectivity.
source_check.problem: The affirmative baseline is stated; the weakness is primarily Vietnamese rather than uniform across languages.

relationships.condition: Gemma-3-4B (Gemma Scope 2) and Qwen3.5-9B; EN, VI, FR, ZH extraction-set inputs
relationships.reason: In r1 and r2, one SAE feature fires on negated inputs with near-zero firing on affirmatives across all four languages. It is a single selected feature, not a prevalence result.
relationships.display_finding: A single SAE feature fired on negated inputs with near-zero firing on affirmatives in all four languages; it is one selected feature, not a measure of prevalence.

relation.reason: Inspection of selected SAE features on unsteered negative and affirmative inputs provides indirect evidence of sparse-feature recovery under V4.

tranche.reason: The multilingual translation setting supplies activation-selectivity results bearing on V4, beyond using SAE features for steering.

source_check.notes: Feature interpretation uses one selected feature per model on synthetic extraction data; dictionary-wide prevalence and a causal effect of base-to-instruct transfer are untested. The authors' conclusion about consistent responses in every language needs the explicit qualification of weak Llama Vietnamese activation.

reader_labels.reason: The selected SAE features respond to negation markers or negated contexts in natural inputs (r1–r2). This is evidence for recoverable sparse features, not for their prevalence or completeness.
